narrative:
The model determined that you have a 40% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the threshold the bank uses, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income, and the level of savings you currently hold. 

Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the denial. Among approved applicants, only about 13% have a negative balance, while the majority (59%) have no checking account at all. This negative status pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk.

Your requested installment rate of 2% of disposable income worked in your favor. It is lower than the 3% average seen among approved loans, which helped pull the prediction back toward approval.

However, having less than 100 DM in savings also increased the risk score. Nearly half of all applicants share this low-savings position, but combined with the negative checking account it still contributed to the unfavorable decision.

In short, the combination of an overdrawn checking account and very limited savings outweighed the positive effect of your lower monthly repayment burden.

What you should do next is focus on clearing your checking account overdraft and building at least a modest cash reserve. Once those two areas improve, reapply. You may also want to explore a smaller loan amount or a longer repayment period to further reduce the monthly burden.
